name: Canada (federal)
legalSystem: common law (federal), bijural with Quebec civil law
note: Deaths are registered under provincial and territorial law. The federal layer learns of them from the provinces: each province's vital statistics agency feeds deaths to ESDC's Social Insurance Register, and provincial offices and the SIR update the CRA automatically. Elections Canada updates the Register of Electors from provincial vital statistics data and from the CRA. Statistics Canada compiles deaths nationally. Families must still report deaths in a territory or abroad, cancel CPP/OAS, and return passports. Canada has no official death-verification service for the private sector.

steps.title: Provincial vital statistics notifies the Social Insurance Register
steps.who: The vital statistics agency of the province where the death occurred, under a data-sharing agreement with Employment and Social Development Canada (Service Canada), which keeps the Social Insurance Register.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death in a province.
steps.summary: For a death in any province, the provincial vital statistics agency notifies the SIN program automatically and the family need do nothing. The statutory basis on the federal side is the Minister's general power to make information-obtaining agreements with provinces; the individual agreements were not found published.

steps.title: Family reports a territorial or foreign death to the SIN program
steps.who: The family or estate, with proof of death (a funeral director's statement of death or the death certificate).
steps.trigger: A death in Yukon, the Northwest Territories, Nunavut, or outside Canada.
steps.summary: The automatic feed covers provinces only. For a death in a territory or abroad, the family must report it to the SIN program, usually by mail or at a Service Canada Centre.

steps.title: Family notifies Service Canada to cancel CPP and OAS
steps.who: The family, executor or estate of a Canada Pension Plan or Old Age Security beneficiary.

deadline.text: as soon as possible; payments after the month of death must be returned

steps.summary: Service Canada still asks the family to report the date of death so that CPP and OAS stop. Every payment issued after the month of death must be returned, which makes the family report the practical trigger even where the SIN record is already updated.

steps.title: Provincial vital statistics and the SIR update the CRA
steps.who: Provincial vital statistics offices directly, and the Social Insurance Register held by ESDC through a data exchange.
steps.trigger: Registration of the death; update of the Social Insurance Register.
steps.summary: The CRA receives death information from provincial vital statistics offices and from the Social Insurance Register, and these records update its database automatically, without a CRA employee keying them in. The source is a 2014 Taxpayers' Ombudsperson report; by then the participating provinces included British Columbia, Quebec, Ontario and New Brunswick.

steps.title: Family reports the date of death to the CRA
steps.who: The legal representative or family, by phone or with Form RC4111 sent to the deceased's tax centre.
steps.trigger: The death; benefit payments (GST/HST credit, Canada Child Benefit) still running.
steps.summary: The CRA's current guidance still tells families to report the date of death, even if the deceased received no benefits. Separately, the legal representative must file the final return. For a death after October and before the normal filing date, it is due six months after the death.

steps.title: Provincial vital statistics data updates the National Register of Electors
steps.who: The Chief Electoral Officer of Canada, drawing on information held under the provincial Acts listed in Schedule 2: every province's Vital Statistics Act, and the Civil Code of Quebec.
steps.trigger: Death registrations made available to Elections Canada under the provincial Acts.
steps.summary: The Register of Electors is updated from information the Chief Electoral Officer considers reliable that is held under a provincial Act listed in Schedule 2. Schedule 2 names each province's vital statistics Act, and the Civil Code for Quebec, so deaths reach the federal register through provincial registrars.

steps.title: CRA supplies details of deceased taxpayers to Elections Canada
steps.who: The Minister of National Revenue, at the request of the Chief Electoral Officer.
steps.trigger: A final return filed for an individual to whom ITA s. 150(1)(b) applies, where the person had authorized sharing with Elections Canada.
steps.summary: On request, the CRA must give Elections Canada the name, date of birth and address of deceased individuals (those for whom a deceased person's return applies) who had consented on their last return. This is a second route to removing the dead from the register.

steps.title: Provincial registrars supply death registrations to Statistics Canada
steps.who: Provincial and territorial vital statistics registrars, for the Canadian Vital Statistics - Death database.
steps.summary: Statistics Canada compiles national mortality statistics from provincial and territorial death registrations. Its statutory access rests on the Statistics Act duty to give the Chief Statistician access to records. The Statistics Canada survey page that describes the feed could not be retrieved.

steps.title: Family returns a valid passport for cancellation
steps.trigger: The death of a holder of a valid Canadian passport.
steps.summary: No automatic cancellation of passports on death was found. The family mails a valid passport to the Passport Program with a copy of the death certificate and asks for it to be destroyed or returned. An expired passport need not be sent.

steps.title: Family notifies the credit bureaus
steps.summary: Canada has no official death-data service for private bodies like the US Death Master File. The Government of Canada tells families to notify the two credit reporting agencies themselves to prevent fraudulent credit checks. Banks and insurers rely on a death certificate or funeral director's statement presented by the estate.

centralPopulationRegister.name: None (the Social Insurance Register is the nearest equivalent)
centralPopulationRegister.note: Canada has no population register. ESDC's Social Insurance Register is updated from provincial death registrations and passes deaths on to the CRA, but other bodies do not read from it as a general register.

governmentPropagation.note: Provincial registrations reach the SIR, the CRA and Elections Canada through data feeds without a family request. Territorial and foreign deaths do not. Service Canada (CPP/OAS), the CRA and the Passport Program still ask families to report, and some steps (passport cancellation) depend on the family.

privateSectorVerification.note: No federal law or service gives banks, insurers or credit bureaus access to death data. The government's own guidance tells families to notify the credit bureaus. A provincial route exists only where a province creates one; none found for private bodies in BC, Ontario or Quebec.

gaps: The ESDC-province data-sharing agreements (the 'Vital Event Linkage' arrangements) that feed provincial deaths to the Social Insurance Register were not found published; only ESDC's public statement that provinces notify automatically and the DESDA s. 41 agreement power were verified.

The CRA's receipt of provincial death data is sourced to a 2014 (archived) Taxpayers' Ombudsperson report. No current CRA statement of the feed was found, and current CRA guidance still asks families to report the date of death.
No published federal rule or system was found that cancels a passport automatically on registration of a death.

No Canadian equivalent of the US Limited Access Death Master File was found. The Canada Pension Plan s. 104.01 ff. and Old Age Security Act information-sharing provisions were not searched for a private-sector route.
Whether CPP/OAS payments stop automatically on the SIR death update (rather than on the family's report) is not stated in the guidance read; Service Canada asks families to notify.
